assessments.zone: Rural villages of Mungindu secteur (Mungindu health zone and northern Gungu health zone areas: Totshi, Mundundu etc.)
assessments.evidence: Rural villages under customary chiefs within state authority, administered by the secteur; any permanent force presence is likely limited to small PNC posts in larger villages (not verified). No source reports armed-group control or regular raids in Mungindu secteur as of the reference date; the Mobondo militia theatre (Kwamouth, Bagata, Kenge, Kwango, western Bulungu) lies well to the west. Live web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted), so the assessment rests on default state presence. Reviewer (2026-10-01) could not run independent searches either; no change in controller, confidence kept low.

units.CD3206-idiofa-3: This unit covers the Mungindu secteur of Idiofa territory (Kwilu), a rural area served by the Mungindu health zone and the northern part of Gungu health zone. No armed group is reported to control or regularly raid any locality here; the Mobondo militia, active in western Kwilu, Kwango and Mai-Ndombe since 2022, operates far to the west. All locations are assessed as under ordinary state authority with the PNC as the main permanent force alongside secteur administration and customary chiefs. Live web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for the secteur seat and low elsewhere.
units.CD3206-idiofa-2: This unit covers the Kimputu, Koshibanda and Mokala secteurs of Idiofa territory (Kwilu), a rural area east of the Kwilu river including the Koshibanda, Kimputu, Mokala, Ipamu, Mukedi and Djuma health zones. No armed group is known to exercise territorial control here; the Mobondo militia active in Kwilu since 2022 has affected mainly western Bagata/Bulungu areas far to the west, and Idiofa has seen only sporadic community/land conflicts and banditry. All localities are assessed as under ordinary state authority with the PNC as main permanent force alongside territorial administration and customary chiefs. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted), so confidence is low for rural villages. A skeptical review (2026-10-01) also could not run web searches (budget exhausted, news sites blocked by proxy); the default-state-presence assessment is retained unverified, consistent with the neighbouring Idiofa and Gungu units.
units.CD3206-idiofa-1: Idiofa territory part 1 (Kwilu) covers Idiofa town and the Idiofa and Ipamu secteurs, including the Kasai river towns of Mangai and Dibaya-Lubwe. No armed group is reported to control or regularly raid any locality here: Radio Okapi coverage of Idiofa, Mangai and Dibaya-Lubwe in 2025-2026 concerns unpaid teachers, electricity, weather and ordinary crime, not militia activity, and the Mobondo militia remains confined to the Maï-Ndombe border areas of Kwilu (Bagata, Bulungu) far to the west, where the government reported it in retreat in March 2026. All locations are assessed as under ordinary state authority, with the PNC and the parquet/courts of Idiofa as the main coercive and justice institutions and customary chiefs under them. Confidence is medium for the main towns and low for villages, as evidence is the absence of reported armed-group activity rather than positive reporting on police posts.
